questions.question: What Prefect-native execution profile guarantees concurrent sibling Stage Parent Flow runs while retaining Stage Flow identity and Root-to-Stage parent/correlation semantics?
questions.evidence: Under four repeated runs with the supported SQLite single-worker API server, sibling Stage Flow overlap occurred in 3/4 runs; one run serialized both child Flows. Root dispatch Task submission does not guarantee child Flow overlap.
requiredProof: Two or more Stage Flow Runs overlap deterministically across repeated runs.
Each Stage remains a native Flow Run with a stable Stage specialization identity.
Root invocation context and parent-child correlation remain available or are explicitly preserved without conflating identities.
Inputs, outputs, failures and completion are observable by the Root Flow.
questions.candidateInvestigation: Qualify process/worker/deployment-backed Prefect Flow invocation only if native hierarchy semantics are preserved. Do not assume run_deployment is equivalent to a native subflow. Prefect API-server multi-worker mode is not supported with SQLite; it requires PostgreSQL.

questions.question: Do any concrete Generator Stage specializations require concurrent sibling Step Subflows?
questions.evidence: Sibling Step Subflows were serialized in all eight Stage sibling pairs across four supported-profile runs.
requiredProof: Derive actual Step membership and dependency/transition semantics from specialized Stage and Step contracts.
Identify which Steps are independent and which are sequential or conditional.
Only where parallel sibling Steps are required, qualify the exact native Prefect pattern and parent correlation.
questions.candidateInvestigation: Do not introduce a general concurrency mechanism or extra hierarchy layer before the concrete Step Composition topology demonstrates a need.

questions.question: Can a worker/deployment-backed Stage Flow invocation preserve the required parent-child identity and result semantics?
questions.evidence: The local direct child-Flow call pattern does not provide deterministic sibling Flow overlap.
requiredProof: Native Stage Flow Run identity and invocation context remain distinct from GPWCF Stage identity.
Root can correlate the dispatched Stage Flow Run and receive its typed result/failure.
No hidden global scheduler or universal adapter is added to GPWCF.
Operational State remains separate from GPWCF domain result.
questions.candidateInvestigation: Compare Prefect run_deployment / worker execution against direct nested Flow calls using an explicit parent invocation envelope; record any loss of native parent_task_run_id as a limitation. If multi-worker API-server mode is evaluated, use a PostgreSQL-backed profile and include its operational/dependency costs.

questions.question: Which Generator Stage branches actually require sibling Stage concurrency?
questions.evidence: The native hierarchy proves Stage invocation but sibling Stage overlap was observed in only three of four runs.
requiredProof: Map STG-01..STG-13 dependencies and branch/fan-in relationships.
Identify actual concurrent Stage pairs from their specialized contracts, not by assumption.
Link each concurrency requirement to the corresponding Prefect execution acceptance test.
